newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bawag to bid for Creditanstalt - paper.
newsitem.headline: Bawag to bid for Creditanstalt - paper.

text.p: Austria's Bank fuer Arbeit und Wirtschaft (Bawag) is poised to make an offer for sell-off candidate Creditanstalt, topping a rival bid by a group led by EA-Generali, daily Der Standard said on Saturday.

Bawag, which is 45 percent owned by Germany's Bayerische Landesbank, would offer 800 schillings per share for all or parts of the government's 70 percent voting stake in the bank, compared to about 720 to 730 schillings per share offered by the Generali-led consortium, it said.
Creditanstalt's ordinary shares closed at 729 schillings on the Vienna bourse on Friday.
Quoting unnamed banking sources, the paper said Finance Minister Viktor Klima was expected to reject Bawag in favour of EA-Generali because of "greater structural effects".

The report came a day after Klima said EA-Generali would complete its due diligence study of Creditanstalt on Monday, while a second, unnamed bidder had decided not to take a closer look at the sell-off candidate.

Analysts widely took that announcement as an indication that the second bidder was either a phantom or had decided to follow a host of domestic and international suitors that have lost interest in the bank over the past few years.
Creditanstalt was first put up for sale in 1991.

Klima earlier this month said he had received two indicative offers for the state's 19.9 million voting shares in the bank, one of which was by EA-Generali and its partners -- including Germany's Commerzbank, savings bank Die Erste and Banca Commerciale Italiana.
Final offers for Creditanstalt, one-time banker to the Austro-Hungarian empire, have to be submitted by December 16. Klima has repeatedly said he wants to wrap up the sale by year-end.
